{'role': 'user', 'content': [{'type': 'text', 'text': '<file name="D:\\dev\\ab-tasks\\_briefs\\raptor\\brief.md">\n# Task Brief: Port Raptor: Call of the Shadows (Sector 1) to HTML5\n\n## 1. Goal\n\nPort *Raptor: Call of the Shadows* (Apogee, 1994) — sector 1 only, the shareware\ncontent — from the original DOS game to a browser game built with HTML5 canvas,\nvanilla JavaScript, and the Web Audio API. The port must render real game assets\n(graphics and sounds) extracted from the original shareware data files, either at\nbuild time or at runtime — no placeholder art, no placeholder audio. Do not use\nany external frameworks or libraries beyond what ships in the browser (no React,\nPhaser, PixiJS, Howler, etc.). A small vanilla test runner is fine if you want\none, but it is not required.\n\n## 2. Worktree Layout\n\nYour worktree root (`./`) contains the GPL C/ASM source of the original DOS game,\nprovided for reference and porting purposes, under `SOURCE/`, `GFX/`, `audiolib/`,\nand `apodmx/`. It also contains the original shareware game data files under\n`./data/` — GLB archive files, the shareware `RAP.EXE` for reference, and whatever\nelse the shareware distribution contained.\n\nBuild your web port as new files alongside/above this existing tree (for example\n`index.html`, an asset-extraction or build script, and your JS source), and keep\nthe original source tree intact for reference — do not delete or rewrite it.\n\nYou must write and maintain a `README` documenting a working dev-server command\n(for example `npx serve .`, `python -m http.server`, or similar) so that the port\ncan be opened and played in a browser at any milestone. Keep this command accurate\nand working as you go — it will be used to check your progress at each milestone.\n\n## 3. Standing Rules\n\n- Vanilla JavaScript + HTML5 canvas + Web Audio API only. No external runtime\n  frameworks or libraries. A lightweight bundler or dev-only tool is fine if it\n  produces plain output, but avoid dependency-heavy tooling.\n- Always leave behind a documented, working dev server command that serves a\n  working build.\n- Commit to git after completing each milestone (M1 through M5, below), so\n  progress is checkpointed.\n- Sector 1 (shareware) content only — you do not need to support later sectors\n  or the registered/full game.\n\n## 4. Milestone Ladder (M1–M5)\n\nThis is the actual grading spec. Copied verbatim:\n\n- **M1**: level-1 background + player ship rendered on canvas from the real GLB\n  data. Graded by screenshot similarity (SSIM) to a reference DOSBox frame on the\n  playfield region (target >= 0.80), and >= 90% of the reference color palette\n  present.\n- **M2**: arrow keys move the ship; firing spawns a projectile.\n- **M3**: wave-1 enemies spawn; a projectile hit decrements enemy HP or removes\n  the enemy; the player can die.\n- **M4**: HUD (score/shields) renders; a Web Audio context is running and at\n  least one sound effect is triggered on firing.\n- **M5**: the sector-1 loop completes — the wave counter advances through wave 9\n  and a sector-complete screen appears.\n\n## 5. Grader Interface Contract\n\nYou **must** implement exactly this. An automated Playwright script checks\nagainst it — this is a hard requirement, not a suggestion.\n\n- A canvas element `<canvas id="raptor-canvas">` whose internal pixel buffer is\n  exactly 320x200 (`canvas.width === 320`, `canvas.height === 200`), independent\n  of any CSS display scaling.\n- Controls: `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` / `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` move the ship;\n  the Space bar fires. Use standard `keydown`/`keyup` DOM listeners — no custom\n  input hook needed.\n- A live-updated global object `window.__raptor` with this exact shape:\n\n  ```js\n  window.__raptor = {\n    ready: boolean,            // true once the first frame (background + player ship) is drawn from real game data\n    player: { x: number, y: number, alive: boolean },\n    projectiles: [ { x: number, y: number, owner: \'player\'|\'enemy\' }, /* ... */ ],\n    enemies: [ { id: string|number, hp: number, x: number, y: number, alive: boolean }, /* ... */ ],\n    hud: { score: number, shields: number },\n    audio: { contextState: \'running\'|\'suspended\'|\'closed\', sfxCount: number },  // sfxCount increments on every SFX triggered\n    wave: number,               // current wave within sector 1\n    sectorComplete: boolean\n  };\n  ```\n\n- Keep this object\'s fields in sync with actual game state at all times. The\n  grader polls it, drives real keyboard input to test M2/M3/M4/M5, and takes a\n  canvas screenshot to test M1. For M5 the grader is allowed to auto-play (hold\n  fire, jitter movement) rather than requiring skilled play, so you do not need\n  to build any special "autoplay" or "god mode" feature — just make the interface\n  accurately reflect real game state during ordinary play.\n\n</file>\n'}], 'attribution': 'user', 'timestamp': 1787283951008}

The key items for the game:\n\n- FILE0000.GLB: text, music, SFX (Apogee Sound System format — .APF? Actually it\'s the old Apogee sound format: a header of 52 bytes containing rate, volume, loop, type, data)\n- FILE0001.GLB:\n  - 0x10000: palette (768 bytes of VGA palette)\n  - 0x10001: SYSTEM_FNT font\n  - 0x10022: BACKGRND_PIC — background image!\n  - Fonts, numbers (N0-N9, N$), SHLDLOW_PIC (shields low?)\n  - SPRITE1_ITM (0x100fc) — sprite library (SPRITE array)\n  - FLATSG1_ITM (0x100fd) — flat library (FLATS array)\n  - MAP1G1_MAP..MAP9G1_MAP (0x100fe-0x10106) — 9 waves of MAZELEVEL data!\n  - SHIP01G1_PIC.. — sprite graphics (GFX_PIC)\n  - STARTG1TILES..ENDG1TILES label — ground tiles (flat graphics)\n\nSo the "waves" are literally 9 MAP files (MAP1G1_MAP - MAP9G1_MAP) — 9 waves per sector! This matches M5\'s "the wave counter advances through wave 9".\n\nThe MAZELEVEL struct contains `map[MAP_SIZE]`, where MAP_SIZE = 150*9 = 1350 MAZEDATA entries, each 4 bytes (2 shorts) = 5400 bytes + 12-byte header. Each MAZEDATA: flats index, fgame.\n\nWait, but MAP_ROWS=150, MAP_COLS=9: the map is a scrolling vertical strip. The playfield is 320x200, and the map scrolls downward (the player flies upward). The visible area is 8x9 = 72 cells? MAP_ONSCREEN=8, MAP_COLS=9. Each cell is 32x32 px. 9 cols * 32 = 288 px = MAP_RIGHT-MAP_LEFT (304-16=288). 8 rows * 32 = 256 > 200-18… hmm, MAP_BOTTOM=182, MAP_TOP=2, height 180 px.\n\nLet me look at RAP.C\'s Do_Game and ENEMY.C to understand wave loading and spawning. The MAZEDATA.flats field references an index into flatlib (FLATS array). FLATS.linkflat is a link to the next cell in the same flat group? Let me actually read ENEMY_C to understand.\n\nAlso, I need to understand how the map scrolls: the game has a "map" that scrolls down as the player advances. The MAP1G1 map has 150 rows of 9 columns. The 8 rows on screen. The top row of the visible window advances with the player\'s y position? Encrypt Data\r\n ***************************************************************************/\r\nVOID\r\nGLB_EnCrypt(\r\nCHAR     *key,             // INPUT : Key that will allow Decryption\r\nBYTE     *buffer,          // INPUT : Buffer to Encrypt\r\nsize_t   length            // INPUT : Length of Buffer\r\n)\r\n{\r\n   INT   klen = strlen( key );\r\n   INT   prev_byte;\r\n   INT   kidx;\r\n  \r\n   kidx = SEED % klen;\r\n   prev_byte = key[ kidx ];\r\n   while ( length-- )\r\n   {\r\n      prev_byte = ( *buffer + key[ kidx ] + prev_byte ) % 256;\r\n      *buffer++ = prev_byte;\r\n  \r\n      if ( ++kidx >= klen )\r\n         kidx = 0;\r\n   }\r\n}\r\n  \r\n/***************************************************************************\r\n  GLB_DeCrypt - Decrypt Data\r\n ***************************************************************************/\r\nVOID\r\nGLB_DeCrypt(\r\nCHAR    *key,               // INPUT : Key that will allow Decryption\r\nBYTE    *buffer,            // INPUT : Buffer to Encrypt\r\nsize_t  length              // INPUT : Length of Buffer\r\n)\r\n{\r\n   INT   klen = strlen( key );\r\n   INT   prev_byte;\r\n   INT   kidx;\r\n   CHAR  dchr;\r\n  \r\n   kidx = SEED % klen;\r\n   prev_byte = key[ kidx ];\r\n   while ( length-- )\r\n   {\r\n      dchr = ( *buffer - key[ kidx ] - prev_byte ) % 256;\r\n      prev_byte = *buffer;\r\n      *buffer++ = dchr;\r\n  \r\n      if ( ++kidx >= klen )\r\n         kidx = 0;\r\n   }\r\n}\r\n\r\n/*------------------------------------------------------------------------\r\n   GLB_FindFile() - Finds a file, opens it, and stores it\'s path \r\n ------------------------------------------------------------------------*/\r\nPRIVATE INT\r\nGLB_FindFile(\r\nINT\treturn_on_failure,\t// INPUT : Don\'t bomb if file not open\r\nINT\tfilenum,             // INPUT : file number\r\nINT\tpermissions\t\t\t\t// INPUT : file access permissions\r\n)\r\n{\r\n   char        *routine = "GLB_FindFile";\r\n   char        filename[ _MAX_PATH ];\r\n   int         handle;\r\n   FILEDESC    *fd;\r\n/*\r\n* Scott, the ASSERT function is a macro that will be compiled-out when\r\n* not debugging ( DEBUG not defined ), otherwise it calls EXIT_Assert\r\n* if the expression is false ( which bails out of your program and displays\r\n* the expression, file & line number of the assertion ).  This is a standard\r\n* way of checking variables for correct boundries during development, and\r\n* makes it easy to remove extra logic for doing so by recompiling without\r\n* DEBUG defined.\r\n*/\r\n   ASSERT( filenum >= 0 && filenum < MAX_GLB_FILES );\r\n/*\r\n* create a file name and attempt to open it local first, then if it\r\n* fails use the exe path and try again.\r\n*/\r\n   sprintf( filename, "%s%04u.glb", prefix, filenum );\r\n   if ( ( handle = open( filename, permissions ) ) == -1 )\r\n\t{\r\n      sprintf( filename, "%s%s%04u.glb", exePath, prefix, filenum );\r\n   \tif ( ( handle = open( filename, permissions ) ) == -1 )\r\n\t\t{\r\n\t\t\tif ( return_on_failure )\r\n\t\t\t\treturn -1;\r\n\r\n         sprintf( filename, "%s%04u.glb", prefix, filenum );\r\n   \t   EXIT_Error ("GLB_FindFile: %s, Error #%d,%s",\r\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\tfilename, errno, strerror( errno ) );\r\n\t\t}\r\n\t}\r\n/*\r\n* Keep file handle\r\n*/\r\n   fd = &filedesc[ filenum ];\r\n\r\n   strcpy( fd->filepath, filename );\r\n   fd->permissions = permissions;\r\n   fd->handle = handle;\r\n\r\n\treturn handle;\r\n}\r\n  \r\n\r\n  \r\n/*------------------------------------------------------------------------\r\n   GLB_OpenFile() - Opens & Caches file handle\r\n ------------------------------------------------------------------------*/\r\nPRIVATE INT\r\nGLB_OpenFile(\r\nINT\treturn_on_failure,\t// INPUT : Don\'t bomb if file not open\r\nINT\tfilenum,             // INPUT : file number\r\nINT\tpermissions\t\t\t\t// INPUT : file access permissions\r\n)\r\n{\r\n   FILEDESC    *fd;\r\n\r\n   ASSERT( filenum >= 0 && filenum < MAX_GLB_FILES );\r\n\r\n   fd = &filedesc[ filenum ];\r\n\r\n   if ( fd->handle == 0 )\r\n      return GLB_FindFile( return_on_failure, filenum, permissions );\r\n   else if ( fd->permissions != permissions )\r\n   {\r\n      close( fd->handle );\r\n   \tif ( ( fd->handle = open( fd->filepath, permissions ) ) == -1 )\r\n\t\t{\r\n\t\t\tif ( return_on_failure )\r\n\t\t\t\treturn -1;\r\n\r\n   \t   EXIT_Error ("GLB_OpenFile: %s, Error #%d,%s",\r\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\tfd->filepath, errno, strerror( errno ) );\r\n      }\r\n   }\r\n   else\r\n   {\r\n      lseek( fd->handle, 0L, SEEK_SET );\r\n   }\r\n   return fd->handle;\r\n}\r\n  \r\n\r\n/*------------------------------------------------------------------------\r\n   GLB_CloseFiles() - Closes all cached files.\r\n ------------------------------------------------------------------------*/\r\nPRIVATE VOID\r\nGLB_CloseFiles(\r\nVOID\r\n)\r\n{\r\n\tINT\t\tj;\r\n\r\n\tfor ( j = 0; j < MAX_GLB_FILES; j++ )\r\n\t{\r\n      if ( filedesc[ j ].handle )\r\n      {\r\n   \t\tclose( filedesc[ j ].handle );\r\n         filedesc[ j ].handle = 0;\r\n      }\r\n\t}\r\n}\r\n\r\n\r\n/*------------------------------------------------------------------------\r\n   GLB_NumItems() - Returns number of items in a .GLB file\r\n ------------------------------------------------------------------------*/\r\nPRIVATE INT\r\nGLB_NumItems (\r\nINT filenum\r\n)\r\n{\r\n   KEYFILE     key;\r\n   INT         handle;\r\n\r\n   ASSERT( filenum >= 0 && filenum < num_glbs );\r\n\r\n\thandle = GLB_OpenFile( 1, filenum, O_RDONLY | O_BINARY );\r\n\tif ( handle == -1 )\r\n\t\treturn 0;\r\n\r\n   lseek( handle, 0L, SEEK_SET );\r\n   if ( ! read( handle,( VOID * ) &key, sizeof( KEYFILE ) ) )\r\n   {\r\n      EXIT_Error( "GLB_NumItems: Read failed!" );\r\n   }\r\n  \r\n#ifdef _SCOTTGAME\r\n   GLB_DeCrypt( serial, ( BYTE * )&key, sizeof( KEYFILE ) );\r\n#endif\r\n  \r\n   return ( ( int ) key.offset );\r\n}\r\n\r\n/*--------------------------------------------------------------------------\r\n GLB_LoadIDT() Loads a item descriptor table from a GLB file.\r\n --------------------------------------------------------------------------*/\r\nPRIVATE VOID\r\nGLB_LoadIDT(\r\nFILEDESC *fd               // INPUT: file to load\r\n)\r\n{\r\n   int      handle;\r\n   int      j;\r\n\tint\t\tk;\r\n\tint \t\tn;\r\n   KEYFILE  key[ 10 ];\r\n   ITEMINFO *ii;\r\n\r\n   handle = fd->handle;\r\n   ii = fd->item;\r\n\r\n   lseek( handle, sizeof( KEYFILE ), SEEK_SET );\r', 'truncated': True, 'truncatedBy': 'lines', 'totalLines': 860, 'totalBytes': 7803, 'outputLines': 300, 'outputBytes': 7803, 'lastLinePartial': False, 'firstLineExceedsLimit': False}, 'totalLines': 860, 'displayContent': {'text': '/****************************************************************************\r\n* GLBapi  - Sound file format (Apogee Sound System, aka "DMX" digital patch format):\n\nThis is the classic 52-byte "Apogee sound" format used in Blakestone/Raptor/Descent 1. From the Apogee "Sound System" documentation (I remember this from the Descent 1 source and from the DMX documentation):\n\n```\nOffset  Size  Field\n0       WORD  size           // Total size of the file\n2       WORD  version        // Format version (0x0111)\n4       WORD  type           // 1=8-bit, 2=8-bit signed, 3=8-bit unsigned, 4=8-bit signed?\n6       WORD  reserved\n8       WORD  volume         // 0-255\n10      WORD  loop           // 0=no loop, 1=loop\n12      WORD  loop_start     // Offset from start of data\n14      WORD  loop_end\n18      DWORD rate           // Sample rate (Hz)\n22      CHAR   name[8]       // Description\n30      WORD   size_of_header // 52 (0x34)\n32      WORD   size_of_data   // Size of data in bytes\n```\n\nTotal = 52 bytes? 32 + 20 = 52. Hmm, 22 + 8 = 30, + 2 + 2 = 34… that would make it 34 bytes, not 52. Let me actually count: 2+2+2+2+2+2+2+2+4+8+2+2 = 32. That doesn\'t make 52 either. {'role': 'assistant', 'content': [{'type': 'thinking', 'thinking': 'New player: FORWARD_GUNS + 3× ENERGY (75 shield) + score 10000.\n\nSo the initial HUD state: score = 10000 → "00010000", shield = 75.\n\nNow I understand well enough. Time to make a plan and start building.\n\n# Architecture Plan\n\n## Asset Pipeline (build time, Node scripts → plain JS data files)\n`tools/extract.js`:\n1. Parse FILE0000.GLB + FILE0001.GLB (with GLB parser).\n2. Decode all needed GFX_PICs into `{w, h, rows: [{x, y, len, px: [..]}]}` or dense `{w, h, px}`.\n3. Decode maps (MAP1..9G1): MAZEDATA array + CSPRITE array.\n4. Decode SPRITE1_ITM (SPRITE library, 131 entries) and FLATSG1_ITM (672 entries).\n5. Decode SFX (digital variants) as 16-bit PCM WAV base64 (or raw samples + rate in JS; the Web Audio API can decode raw with AudioBuffer — no WAV needed: create AudioBuffer directly).\n6. Palette (768 bytes), fonts, numbers, shield icons, etc.\n\nOutput files (vanilla JS, no build step needed at runtime):\n- `assets/data.js` → sets `window.__RPT_DATA = {...}` containing everything as JSON or typed array literals. FILE0001.GLB is about 562KB; extracted data might be about 1–2MB of JS. Fine for a browser.\n\nActually simpler: output a single `assets/data.json` + `data.js`? Fetching JSON is cleaner: `fetch(\'assets/data.json\')`. But a dev server is needed anyway (brief expects a dev server command). Use `npx serve .` or python http.server. i < this.numItems; i++) {\n      const off = 28 + i * 28;\n      const rec = Buffer.from(data.subarray(off, off + 28));\n      decrypt(rec, KEY);\n      const v = new DataView(rec.buffer, rec.byteOffset, 28);\n      const nm = rec.toString(\'latin1\', 12, 28).replace(/\\0.*$/, \'\');\n      this.items.push({\n        opt: v.getUint32(0, true),\n        offset: v.getUint32(4, true),\n        size: v.getUint32(8, true),\n        name: nm,\n        encoded: v.getUint32(0, true) === 1,\n      });\n    }\n  }\n  fetch(it) {\n    let buf = Buffer.from(this.data.subarray(it.offset, it.offset + it.size));\n    if (it.encoded) decrypt(buf, KEY);\n    return buf;\n  }\n  get(nameOrNum) {\n    const it = typeof nameOrNum === \'number\'\n      ? this.items[nameOrNum]\n      : this.items.find((x) => x.name === nameOrNum);\n    return it ? this.fetch(it) : null;\n  }\n  indexOf(name) {\n    return this.items.findIndex((x) => x.name === name);\n  }\n}\n\nmodule.exports = { GLB, decrypt, KEY };\n\nif (require.main === module) {\n  const [file, ...args] = process.argv.slice(2);\n  const data = fs.readFileSync(file);\n  const glb = new GLB(data);\n  console.log(`items: ${glb.numItems}`);\n  if (!args.length) {\n    for (let i = 0; Next, write `tools/extract.js`.\n\nDesign of `assets/raptor.bin` + `assets/index.json`:\n\nindex.json:\n```json\n{\n  "palette": [768 bytes as array],\n  "bin": {\n    "name": "raptor.bin",\n    "entries": {\n       "LPLAYER_PIC": {"off": n, "size": m, "w": .., "h": .., "type": 0|1, "file": 0},\n       ...\n    }\n  },\n  "sfx": { "GUN": {"off":..., "rate":11025, "len":...}, ... }\n}\n```\nHmm — sfx can go inside the same bin as an entry with kind:"sfx". Keep a single entry table keyed by name:\n- kind: "gfx" (raw GFX_PIC bytes), "sfx" (raw: 8B header + pcm), "map" (raw MAZEDATA), "lib" (raw), "font" (raw font bytes), "pal", "text".\nEverything is just raw item bytes stored in order; the runtime decodes per kind based on name/kind hints.\n\nEntry naming: for FILE0000, items that have no name get a name from the label: use label names where they exist; for unnamed data items between labels, generate a name like "FX0091" (item number in hex). The runtime looks up what it needs by name:\n- Sprites: exact names from FILE0000.INC / FILE0001.INC (LPLAYER_PIC, NMSHOT_BLK, ESHOT_BLK, BONUS00_PIC, GEXPLO_BLK, SMFLAK_BLK, BOOM_PIC, SPLAT_BLK, BIGSPLAT_BLK, LGFLAK_BLK, EXPLO2_BLK, AIRBOOM_PIC, NRGBANG_BLK, LRBLST_BLK, SSMOKE_BLK, SMOKTRAL_BLK, LGHTIN_BLK, BSPARK_BLK, OSPARK_BLK, GUNSTR_BLK, FLARE_PIC, SPARKLE_PIC, SHIPGLOW_BLK, ELASEPOW_BLK, DETHPOW_BLK, LASERPOW_BLK, DRAYHIT_BLK, PLASMA_BLK, MICROM_BLK, MISDUM_BLK, MISRAT_BLK, MISGRD_BLK, BLDGBOMB_PIC, POWDIS_BLK, MEGABM_BLK, SHOKWV_BLK, FRNTLAS_BLK, DETHRY_BLK, EMISLE_BLK, MINE_BLK, ELASER_BLK, EPLASMA_PIC, COCONUT_PIC, ICNGLW_BLK, SHLDLOW_PIC, WEPDEST_PIC, SMSHIELD_PIC, SMBOMB_PIC, N0_PIC..N9_PIC, NS_PIC, STARTG1TILES.., SPRITE1_ITM..SPRITE4_ITM, FLATSG1_ITM..FLATSG4_ITM, MAP1G1_MAP..MAP9G1_MAP, PALETTE_DAT, SYSTEM_FNT, GAME_FNT, FONT1_FNT, FONT2_FNT, END0_TXT.., ORDER_TXT, LPLAYER_PIC+? — note: frames of LPLAYER_PIC are separate items LPLAYER_PIC..LPLAYER_PIC+6 (7 items: 0x11a..0x120? From FILE0001.INC: LPLAYER_PIC 0x11a=282; +1..+6 = 283..288 — do these have names? In the .INC, only the first one is defined (LPLAYER_PIC). The others are unnamed items. So we have to include unnamed items and name them by index.\n\nTherefore: the extractor includes all items from both GLBs except music, and names unnamed items as "f0_XXXX" / "f1_XXXX" (file + hex item number). The index records all entries by name, and the runtime code references frames by the base name and +1..n computed from the item index (the index also stores the numeric item index: "idx": 282 → frame item name = f0/f1 name of idx+1...). Better approach: the extractor generates explicit names for all frames of known block bases: for a base B with F frames (known list), include items B..B+F-1 under names like "LPLAYER_PIC+1"? JSON keys can be anything. Cleaner: entries keyed by base name, with a "frames": [ {off, size}, ... ] array? The sizes/offsets are contiguous per item in my bin.\n\nThe simplest, most robust approach: an entries array (not object):\n```\n"items": [ {name, idx, off, size, kind, w, h, rate?} ... ]\n```\nPlus a "names" map: name → array index into items. And for frame sequences, the runtime uses item-index lookup: the index map is by name; frames of LPLAYER_PIC: the extractor adds explicit map entries: "LPLAYER_PIC_0".."LPLAYER_PIC_6"? That requires hardcoding the frame counts — no problem, I know them (player 7, NMSHOT 4, etc.). Actually, a simpler generic method: for every named block base in the .INC that is followed by unnamed items, the extractor automatically adds entries: if an unnamed item\'s index is between named label N (idx i) and the next named item (idx j), name it `<N>+<k>` (k = idx-i). Example: LPLAYER_PIC+1, LPLAYER_PIC+4 (player frames 1..4 = LPLAYER_PIC+1..+4? wait, frames: LPLAYER_PIC+0..+6 are 7 items — but item 289 (LPLAYER_PIC+7) is a different sprite? In the .INC: after LPLAYER_PIC 0x11a there\'s SHIP01G1_PIC 0x11f=287 → so LPLAYER_PIC+0..+5 (6 frames: 282..286), then 287 = SHIP01G1_PIC. Hmm! 6 frames? But the ship has 7 pics (0..6). Let me recheck FILE0001.INC: LPLAYER_PIC 0x11a (282), SHIP01G1_PIC 0x11f (287) → 287-282 = 5 → frames 0..4 (5 items). Hmm, but playerpic goes 0..6 (7 values: 0,1,2,3,4,5,6). And SHIP01G1_PIC 0x11f, next? Let me look at the FILE0001.INC listing around those entries. From the earlier archive: "LPLAYER_PIC 0x11a //ITEM:282" "SHIP01G1_PIC 0x11f //ITEM:287". And curship[loop] = LPLAYER_PIC + loop for loop 0..6 → LPLAYER_PIC+5 = 287 = SHIP01G1_PIC, +6 = 288! Every entry is raw\n// (decrypted) item bytes in its original format:\n//   kind "gfx"  : GFX_PIC sprite/dense pic (see index for w/h)\n//   kind "sfx"  : Apogee 8-bit PCM: {type u16, rate u16, dsz u32, samples}\n//   kind "pal"  : 768-byte VGA palette\n//   kind "font" : FONT {height i32, charofs[256] i16, width[256] i8} + char data\n//   kind "map"  : MAZEDATA {size u32, spriteoff u32, numsprites u32, map[1350] u32, csprite[n] 24B}\n//   kind "lib"  : 131 x 528B SPRITE records\n//   kind "flat" : 672 x 8B FLATS records\n//   kind "text" : raw text item\n//   kind "raw"  : anything else (PC-speaker SFX variants etc.), included for completeness\n//\n// Naming: named items keep their GLB name; unnamed items following a named\n// label "X" are named "X+1", "X+2", ... (FX data items, sprite frame runs).\n// Items in the ranges of *_MUS labels (DMX music) are skipped.\n\nconst fs = require(\'fs\');\nconst path = require(\'path\');\nconst { GLB } = require(\'./glbparse.js\');\n\nconst ROOT = path.join(__dirname, \'..\');\nconst OUT = path.join(ROOT, \'assets\');\n\nfunction isNamed(n) {\n  return /^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$/.test(n) && !/^\\d+$/.test(n);\n}\n\nfunction decodeGfx(buf) {\n  if (buf.length < 20) return null;\n  const v = new DataView(buf.buffer, buf.byteOffset, 20);\n  const type = v.getUint32(0, true);\n  const w = v.getInt32(12, true);\n  const h = v.getInt32(16, true);\n  if (type === 1) {\n    if (buf.length !== 20 + w * h) return null;\n    return { w, h };\n  }\n  if (type === 0) {\n    let p = 20;\n    while (true) {\n      if (p + 16 > buf.length) return null;\n      const len = v32(buf, p + 12);\n      const off = v32(buf, p + 8);\n      if (off === 0xffffffff) { p += 16; break; }\n      p += 16 + len;\n      if (p > buf.length) return null;\n    }\n    return { w, h };\n  }\n  return null;\n}\nfunction v32(buf, o) {\n  return buf.readUInt32LE(o);\n}\n\nfunction build(file) {\n  const glb = new GLB(fs.readFileSync(file));\n  const entries = []; // {name, idx, buf, kind, w, h, rate, dsz}\n  let lastLabel = null;\n  let labelIdx = -1;\n  let inMusic = false;\n\n  for (let i = 0; i < glb.items.length; i++) {\n    const it = glb.items[i];\n    const named = isNamed(it.name);\n    if (named) {\n      lastLabel = it.name;\n      labelIdx = i;\n      inMusic = it.name.endsWith(\'_MUS\');\n      if (it.size === 0) continue; // pure label entry\n    }\n    if (inMusic) continue; // skip DMX music data\n    if (it.size === 0) continue;\n    let name;\n    if (named) name = it.name;\n    else if (lastLabel) name = lastLabel + \'+\' + (i - labelIdx);\n    else name = \'UNK_\' + i.toString(16);\n\n    const buf = glb.fetch(it);\n    const e = { name, idx: i, buf };\n    const m = /^([A-Za-z0-9_]+_FX)\\+(\\d+)$/.exec(name);\n    if (m) {\n      // FX group data items; the 4th is the 11025Hz 8-bit digital sample\n      if (buf.length >= 8) {\n        const f0 = buf.readUInt16LE(0);\n        const rate = buf.readUInt16LE(2);\n        const dsz = buf.readUInt32LE(4);\n        if (f0 === 3 && rate >= 8000 && rate <= 24000 && 8 + dsz === buf.length) {\n          e.kind = \'sfx\'; e.rate = rate; e.dsz = dsz;\n        } else {\n          e.kind = \'raw\';\n        }\n      } else e.kind = \'raw\';\n    } else if (name === \'PALETTE_DAT\' && buf.length === 768) {\n      e.kind = \'pal\';\n    } else if (/_FNT$/.test(name)) {\n      e.kind = \'font\';\n    } else if (/^MAP\\dG\\d_MAP$/.test(name)) {\n      e.kind = \'map\';\n    } else if (/^SPRITE\\d_ITM$/.test(name)) {\n      e.kind = \'lib\';\n    } else if (/^FLATSG\\d_ITM$/.test(name)) {\n      e.kind = \'flat\';\n    } else if (/_TXT$/.test(name) || /_DIZ$/.test(name) || /_DIX$/.test(name)) {\n      e.kind = \'text\';\n    } else {\n      const g = decodeGfx(buf);\n      if (g) { e.kind = \'gfx\'; e.w = g.w; e.h = g.h; }\n      else e.kind = \'raw\';\n    }\n    entries.push(e);\n  }\n  return entries;\n}\n\nconst f000 = build(path.join(ROOT, \'data/FILE0000.GLB\'));\nconst f001 = build(path.join(ROOT, \'data/FILE0001.GLB\'));\nconst entries = [...f000, ...f001];\n\n// sanity checks for things the game code needs\nconst need = [\n  \'LPLAYER_PIC\', \'LPLAYER_PIC+1\', \'LPLAYER_PIC+2\', \'LPLAYER_PIC+3\', \'LPLAYER_PIC+4\',\n  \'SHIP01G1_PIC\',
